content.value_statement: Angular projects often mix legacy modules, RxJS-heavy state, and outdated rendering patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward modern Angular practices.
actual_capabilities: Explain and apply Angular Signals for local and derived state.
Guide standalone component setup and lazy route loading.
Show zoneless change detection and SSR hydration patterns.
Recommend modern dependency injection, routing, and form patterns.
Provide testing examples for signal components and signal inputs.
Summarize migration choices from NgModules and legacy decorators.
limitations: Focuses on Angular v20+; legacy AngularJS migration is out of scope.
Does not inspect a repository unless the user provides project files.
Examples need adaptation to each build, API, and deployment environment.
Signal Forms coverage is preview-oriented because the skill treats it as v22+.

use_cases.title: Modernize Component Architecture
use_cases.description: Convert NgModule-based features into standalone components with signal inputs and direct imports.

use_cases.title: Plan Angular Performance Work
use_cases.description: Evaluate zoneless change detection, defer blocks, hydration, and image optimization for a roadmap.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Changes
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code Angular-specific direction before implementation or review.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Modern Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Angular concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Angular Signals fit this component. Use simple steps and note when RxJS is still better.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration for a focused feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Angular component and suggest a migration to standalone components and Signals. Explain each change in simple steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Rendering Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for SSR, hydration, or lazy loading.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular page for performance. Recommend zoneless setup, defer blocks, hydration choices, and tests that should pass.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture planning across an application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a modernization plan for a large Angular application that still uses NgModules and default change detection. Include phases, risks, tests, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to improve an Angular route configuration.
output: A short review explains lazy route loading, functional guards, and resolver placement.
It lists testing checks for navigation and authentication behavior.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to replace local RxJS state in a component.
output: The response identifies state that fits Signals and state that should stay in streams.
It proposes a small migration sequence with validation steps.

output_examples.input: A lead asks whether to enable zoneless Angular for a new app.
output: The response compares benefits, prerequisites, and compatibility risks.
It recommends a test plan before production rollout.

best_practices: Provide the Angular version and relevant project files before asking for implementation help.
Ask for tests when changing routing, hydration, forms, or state management.
Use the skill for focused Angular guidance, then validate changes in the real project.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for AngularJS migration planning.
Do not ask for broad rewrites without clear success criteria.
Do not copy examples into production without adapting APIs, types, and tests.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets modern Angular v20+ patterns, including Signals, standalone components, zoneless setup, SSR, and hydration.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from NgModules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide migration toward standalone components and direct imports for modern Angular applications.

faq.question: Does it replace project-specific testing?
faq.answer: No. The guidance must be validated with the project build, tests, and deployment environment.

faq.question: Can it design SSR and hydration changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Angular SSR setup, client hydration, incremental hydration, and related troubleshooting checks.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they assist with Angular work.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the Angular version, target files, current behavior, desired behavior, and any test or deployment constraints.
